Research & Engineering Lineage · Evolved-SSD

Systems Engineering

The durable inheritance is lifecycle coherence: keep intent, architecture, interfaces, configuration, integration and evidence mutually intelligible as the system and its context change—without imposing a fixed lifecycle or document regime.

Current scientific findings

The lineage draws on industrial systems engineering, systems analysis, requirements, lifecycle practice, model credibility and sociotechnical work. Its current 72-property study asks which relation a decision actually needs. It permits focused partial contributions: a geometric constraint can reject an oversized design while thermal suitability remains unknown.

Read the full current Systems Engineering account · Four current family accounts · Scientific sources and limits

Questions the study addresses

  • Do intent and requirements concern the actual stakeholders, use and legitimate decision authority?
  • Do interfaces agree on units, timing, state, resources and operational meaning?
  • Which change affects which evidence claim, and when is a direct retest cheaper than a reuse argument?

Different predicates require different evidence

A clear requirement can still be unauthorized, infeasible or irrelevant. Trace density is not semantic accuracy. Architecture decomposes work but shared power, clocks, bandwidth and attention can reconnect the parts. No change, reuse, manual work and simplifying the objective remain alternatives.

Interface meaning is operational

The Mars Climate Orbiter record already contained a metric requirement; the issue concerned actual numerical meaning and handoffs. Another unit label alone would not establish compatibility. Ariane 501 illustrates shared software and transferred trajectory assumptions, without proving that every test requires all real hardware.

Configuration-specific reuse

As-designed, as-built, as-tested and as-operated states can differ. Exact bytes do not establish calibration or physical correspondence. A proven display-label-only change can leave thermal evidence valid, changed power can invalidate it, and an unknown dependency remains unknown.

Correct evidence classification

The S117 correction treats stated schedule gains from a qualitative workflow model as modeled results under assumptions, not measurements after deployed transformation. Verification, intended-use validation, contractual acceptance and qualification remain distinct. Nine examined novelty proposals admit no new property.

A supported example and its conditions

A short linked rationale can serve a known local maintenance change without constructing enterprise-wide traceability. A prototype can have positive prospective information value even when its realized observation leaves the action unchanged. Such examples support their actual decision scope, not a general economic effect.

Negative findings, uncertainty and limits

Catalogue-only standards access, selected passages, unresolved native source locators and unbound historical executed-commission evidence remain explicit. Thirteen deterministic author cases are discriminators rather than held-out trials. The historical 72-row body below remains distinct from the selected current 72-row account.

Existing engineering responsibilities

The receiving record names R002D / #197 as the existing Systems Engineering owner. R001F, R000E/R0024, R0022 and R0023 retain work-order, currentness, capacity and acceptance concerns. A future check should ask whether intended use, interfaces, configuration and evidence really correspond; a justified direct observation or focused test can support no change.

These are preliminary routes for a future exact consumer. Research acceptance does not establish a current native defect, appoint an owner or require implementation. Adequate controls, smaller methods and no change remain legitimate outcomes.

Genealogy

  1. Large telecommunications and industrial systems established the problem of coordinating whole-system performance and interfaces beyond component optimisation. Early book-length treatments by Goode and Machol and by Hall joined objectives, alternatives, analysis and coordinated design; neither supplies a single-inventor story.
  2. Post-war systems analysis and operations research contributed explicit comparison of large alternatives under cost, effectiveness and uncertainty. That ancestry supports problem framing and trade studies, but not lifecycle configuration, integration or verification by itself.
  3. Missile, aerospace and space programmes made configuration identity, supplier interfaces, integration and evidence consequential across many specialised organisations. Their high-consequence acquisition machinery is a historical source, not a universal default.
  4. Requirements engineering, systems architecting, interface and configuration control, and verification and validation developed as overlapping specialist traditions. Concurrent engineering reacted to slow sequential hand-offs; systems-of-systems work addressed constituents that retain independent management and operation.
  5. Model-based systems engineering, SysML and digital engineering later made relations more structured, queryable and machine-readable. They extend the tradition only when model semantics, configuration parity, credibility, portability and a live decision consumer are governed.
  6. Software, agile and continuous-delivery practice translated the coherence problem towards faster feedback and executable evidence. Physical irreversibility, long-lead items, qualification and supplier boundaries still prevent universal transfer of software cadence.

Mäder and Egyed, maintenance-task traceability study, and Ruiz, Hu and Dalpiaz, practice-barrier studyMaintained traceability can help bounded maintenance tasks, while cost, tools and collaboration make it difficult to sustain.That maximal link coverage is always beneficial, semantically correct or transferable to every system type.
Henderson and Salado, MBSE benefits reviewMost reviewed benefit claims were perceived rather than measured, with inconclusive aggregate evidence.That MBSE never helps, or that proprietary programme evidence has been exhaustively observed.

What survives after criticism

The surviving centre is authoritative but revisable intent, with verification and validation kept distinct: the familiar V&V shorthand cannot promote evidence from one question into the other.

Systems engineering contributes a conditional coherence loop. Authoritative stakeholder or mission intent informs requirements and assumptions; architecture records consequential choices and alternatives; interfaces state behaviour, timing, units, state and failure semantics; configuration identifies what was built and tested; integration exposes composition effects; verification checks a specified claim; validation asks whether the result remains fit for its intended use. Change then reopens only the relations and evidence it can invalidate.

  • Ground intent in current, named authority and separate the need from a preferred solution.
  • Treat assumptions as owned, testable and expiring claims, not invisible premises.
  • Record architecture decisions and rejected alternatives; diagrams are optional views.
  • Give interfaces explicit ownership and verify their semantic and configuration currentness across the real boundary.
  • Bind baselines and evidence to the exact product, model, test data, environment and intended use.
  • Integrate early at risky boundaries and feed anomalies back into requirements and architecture.
  • Scale modelling, traceability, review and assurance to consequence, coupling, uncertainty, distribution, irreversibility and evidence fragility; keep a cheap path for local reversible work.

Criticism materially changed the tradition. Frozen requirements became progressive, revisable baselines; traceability became consumer-driven rather than link-maximal; architecture shifted from approved pictures towards decisions, rationale and scenarios; interface control expanded beyond signatures to semantics and composition evidence; and static artefacts became versioned relations with currentness and invalidation rules.

The tensions remain real. Decomposition can hide emergent interactions. A baseline can preserve identity or become gatekeeping. Early integration reduces late surprise but may be physically costly or destructive. Formal models improve analysis while increasing specialist dependence and false authority. Federated systems may have no actor able to enforce a global plan. These are triggers for explicit assumptions and proportional assurance, not reasons to universalise a heavyweight method.

How IMPLEMENTAUDIT translates it

IMPLEMENTAUDIT translates the coherence loop into existing repository-native controls: owner/source and intended outcome before work; assumptions and acceptance in phase design; exact repository, package and environment identity; dependency and interface checks; baseline-versus-final comparison; claim-specific evidence; a handoff recipient reconstructing state from live sources; change-sensitive invalidation; and a final distinction between technical evidence, authorised acceptance and public readback.

The accepted original v0.4 crosswalk records no new v0.4 runtime change for any of the 72 Systems Engineering rows. Its architectural relations instead confirm that the v0.4 decomposition shows only the detail a decision needs, keeps a package as one exactly identified unit, parallelises only genuinely independent work, forms dependent conclusions only after all required current inputs arrive, lets new evidence reopen earlier decisions, and prevents model advice from becoming decision authority. They are not evidence that a new systems-engineering method was implemented or that every external property is active in every run.

What was already native

The durable audit record, named owner/source, scoped goal, phase acceptance, exact state identity, before/after checks, independent challenge, rollback, handoff reconstruction and evidence-bounded closure already carried much of this lineage. The crosswalk frequently resolves a property through several existing owners because coherence is compositional: for example, intent needs planning and authority; current evidence needs configuration identity and change propagation; and validation needs both observed behaviour and an intended-use consumer.

That composition matters. A green check cannot silently become validation, an approval cannot manufacture technical truth, and a transmitted handoff cannot establish that the receiver still sees the same live state.

What was deliberately not imported

No Systems Engineering mode, fixed V-model, one-pass lifecycle, complete up-front requirements set, mandatory review board, central change board, SysML mandate, digital twin, universal traceability matrix, weighted scorecard or fixed document set was added. An interface-control signature, model element count, review event or compliance status is not treated as the underlying property.

For a small reversible task, the mature form may be a dated goal, one or two decisive assumptions, an immutable build identity, a focused test and direct user confirmation. More machinery is warranted only when a named consequence or failure mode makes it informative.

Tensions, assumptions and evidence limits

Whole-discipline effectiveness evidence is dominated by standards, handbooks, cases, observational comparisons and self-report. Mishap reports establish particular mechanisms, not universal rates. Traceability findings are task-sensitive; MBSE and digital-engineering benefits remain case-heavy and weakly replicated; acquisition outcomes mix engineering with funding, incentives, governance and industrial-base effects. Systems-of-systems and mission-engineering evidence is substantially defence and aerospace shaped.

This route does not establish standards conformance, certification, architectural correctness, complete traceability, model truth, digital-twin fidelity, autonomous AI authority, cross-repository effectiveness or a universal return on investment. Source checks, packaged artefacts, installed behaviour, deployed systems and public state remain different evidence layers.

P001

Property name

Historical origin

Hall's problem-definition and goal-setting tradition; NASA stakeholder-expectations practice; requirements-engineering work on environment and agreement.

Lineage class

DIRECT_SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_LINEAGE

Tradition relation

SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

Original form

Identify customer objectives and translate them into system goals before detailed design.

Problem it addressed

Component teams can optimise a technically impressive solution that does not solve the governing mission or current stakeholder problem.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Solution success is asserted against an unauthorised, stale or internally invented notion of value.

Mechanism

Record the intended outcomes, sources, decision authority, conflicts, use context, assumptions and current validation evidence; make downstream decisions point back to that governed intent.

Trigger or context

Multiple stakeholders; costly or irreversible design; regulated/contractual commitments; uncertain mission; long lifecycle; changed operating context.

Non trigger or cheap path

For a small reversible task with one empowered user and immediate feedback, a dated goal statement plus direct confirmation is enough.

Dependencies or preconditions

Access to representative stakeholders or mission evidence; explicit system boundary and intended lifecycle; a means to resolve or preserve disagreement.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

The governing need, stakeholder classes, intended use and current context must be identifiable; latent/absent stakeholders are a declared limitation.

Authority preconditions

A named person, body, law, contract or mission authority must be able to legitimise or change the governing intent; facilitation is not authority.

Configuration or identity preconditions

The intent record, source and applicable system/configuration/time horizon must be versioned.

Interface or integration preconditions

External actors, environments and ecosystem dependencies that affect intent must be within scope.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Validation evidence must be capable of challenging the stated need and intended-use model.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Solution success is asserted against an unauthorised, stale or internally invented notion of value. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Mission owner, product owner, architecture authority, requirements authority and validation authority.

Known failure modes

Solution-biased framing; token stakeholder participation; stale authority; proxy outcomes; hidden conflicts; retrospective rationalisation.

Important criticisms

Stakeholder workshops and CONOPS documents can create consensus theatre; stated requests may reflect politics, solution bias or absent users.

How the property evolved

Original form: Identify customer objectives and translate them into system goals before detailed design. Evolved under criticism into: A living intent model whose authority, recency, conflicts, measures and affected decisions are explicit; revalidate after material change.

Evolved form in this source

A living intent model whose authority, recency, conflicts, measures and affected decisions are explicit; revalidate after material change.

Ceremony vs property

CONOPS, mission statements, stakeholder registers and workshops are optional carriers. The property is current, authoritative intent that governs and can be challenged.

Original form

Problem it addressed

Failure mode it tries to prevent

P003 — Map stakeholder authority, conflicts and lifecycle standing
Property id

P003

Property name

Map stakeholder authority, conflicts and lifecycle standing

Historical origin

Bell Labs/Hall socio-technical framing; NASA stakeholder identification; requirements agreement research.

Lineage class

DIRECT_SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_LINEAGE

Tradition relation

SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

Original form

List customers, users, operators and programme authorities.

Problem it addressed

A loud requester or contract proxy is treated as the sole legitimate stakeholder while operators, maintainers, regulators or affected parties are ignored.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Conflicts are hidden inside ambiguous requirements and reappear as late acceptance or operational failure.

Mechanism

For each stakeholder, identify role, decision rights, obligations, represented populations, conflict-resolution authority and lifecycle phase.

Trigger or context

Distributed ownership; multiple customer classes; safety/regulatory duties; operator/maintainer burden; systems of systems.

Non trigger or cheap path

Single-user reversible work can use direct owner confirmation without a formal register.

Dependencies or preconditions

Access to representative stakeholders or mission evidence; explicit system boundary and intended lifecycle; a means to resolve or preserve disagreement.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

The governing need, stakeholder classes, intended use and current context must be identifiable; latent/absent stakeholders are a declared limitation.

Authority preconditions

A named person, body, law, contract or mission authority must be able to legitimise or change the governing intent; facilitation is not authority.

Configuration or identity preconditions

The intent record, source and applicable system/configuration/time horizon must be versioned.

Interface or integration preconditions

External actors, environments and ecosystem dependencies that affect intent must be within scope.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Validation evidence must be capable of challenging the stated need and intended-use model.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Conflicts are hidden inside ambiguous requirements and reappear as late acceptance or operational failure. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Mission owner, product owner, architecture authority, requirements authority and validation authority.

Known failure modes

Solution-biased framing; token stakeholder participation; stale authority; proxy outcomes; hidden conflicts; retrospective rationalisation.

Important criticisms

Stakeholder mapping can legitimise whoever was easiest to interview and can manufacture false consensus.

How the property evolved

Original form: List customers, users, operators and programme authorities. Evolved under criticism into: A challengeable authority map, not a contact list; unresolved conflicts remain visible and constrain baselining.

Evolved form in this source

A challengeable authority map, not a contact list; unresolved conflicts remain visible and constrain baselining.

Ceremony vs property

CONOPS, mission statements, stakeholder registers and workshops are optional carriers. The property is current, authoritative intent that governs and can be challenged.

INTENT_OR_REQUIREMENTS_PROPERTY

P004 — Model intended use, operational states and environment
Property id

P004

Property name

Model intended use, operational states and environment

Historical origin

CONOPS/operational-concept traditions in aerospace and defence; NASA stakeholder-expectations and validation processes.

Lineage class

AEROSPACE_OR_DEFENCE_LINEAGE

Tradition relation

SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

Original form

Describe missions, operational scenarios, environments, users and support concepts.

Problem it addressed

Requirements are locally correct but omit the conditions, modes, transitions, actors or degraded situations in which the system must work.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Acceptance testing exercises a laboratory abstraction rather than the operational problem.

Mechanism

Use scenarios, mission threads, states/modes, environmental envelopes and lifecycle operations to expose interactions and validation conditions.

Trigger or context

Context-sensitive behaviour; many modes; human/organisational interaction; remote or hazardous operation; degraded states.

Non trigger or cheap path

For simple products, a handful of concrete usage examples and explicit environment bounds may replace a formal CONOPS.

Dependencies or preconditions

Access to representative stakeholders or mission evidence; explicit system boundary and intended lifecycle; a means to resolve or preserve disagreement.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

The governing need, stakeholder classes, intended use and current context must be identifiable; latent/absent stakeholders are a declared limitation.

Authority preconditions

A named person, body, law, contract or mission authority must be able to legitimise or change the governing intent; facilitation is not authority.

Configuration or identity preconditions

The intent record, source and applicable system/configuration/time horizon must be versioned.

Interface or integration preconditions

External actors, environments and ecosystem dependencies that affect intent must be within scope.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Validation evidence must be capable of challenging the stated need and intended-use model.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Acceptance testing exercises a laboratory abstraction rather than the operational problem. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Mission owner, product owner, architecture authority, requirements authority and validation authority.

Known failure modes

Solution-biased framing; token stakeholder participation; stale authority; proxy outcomes; hidden conflicts; retrospective rationalisation.

Important criticisms

Operational documents become speculative narratives when not checked with real users or evidence; exhaustive scenario catalogues are impossible.

How the property evolved

Original form: Describe missions, operational scenarios, environments, users and support concepts. Evolved under criticism into: A maintained operational/use-context model tied to requirements, architecture, interfaces and validation evidence; format is optional.

Evolved form in this source

A maintained operational/use-context model tied to requirements, architecture, interfaces and validation evidence; format is optional.

Ceremony vs property

CONOPS, mission statements, stakeholder registers and workshops are optional carriers. The property is current, authoritative intent that governs and can be challenged.

P005 — Govern outcome, mission and effectiveness measures
Property id

P005

Property name

Govern outcome, mission and effectiveness measures

Historical origin

Systems analysis and early SE effectiveness evaluation; NASA measures of effectiveness and mission engineering.

Lineage class

SYSTEMS_ANALYSIS_ANCESTRY

Tradition relation

SYSTEMS_ANALYSIS_IMPORT_OR_ANCESTRY

Original form

Define quantitative objectives and effectiveness criteria for comparing candidate systems.

Problem it addressed

Teams optimise easy technical proxies that are disconnected from mission outcomes or whose thresholds no longer reflect stakeholder value.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

A dashboard stays green while the delivered capability remains unusable or strategically irrelevant.

Mechanism

Tie each outcome measure to a named stakeholder/mission claim, decision, threshold/objective, measurement context, uncertainty and refresh condition.

Trigger or context

Architecture trades; mission/capability portfolios; performance competition; changing operational priorities.

Non trigger or cheap path

Where direct user feedback immediately settles value, use it instead of constructing a metric hierarchy.

Dependencies or preconditions

Access to representative stakeholders or mission evidence; explicit system boundary and intended lifecycle; a means to resolve or preserve disagreement.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

The governing need, stakeholder classes, intended use and current context must be identifiable; latent/absent stakeholders are a declared limitation.

Authority preconditions

Configuration or identity preconditions

The intent record, source and applicable system/configuration/time horizon must be versioned.

Interface or integration preconditions

External actors, environments and ecosystem dependencies that affect intent must be within scope.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Validation evidence must be capable of challenging the stated need and intended-use model.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: A dashboard stays green while the delivered capability remains unusable or strategically irrelevant. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Mission owner, product owner, architecture authority, requirements authority and validation authority.

Known failure modes

Solution-biased framing; token stakeholder participation; stale authority; proxy outcomes; hidden conflicts; retrospective rationalisation.

Important criticisms

Goodhart effects, proxy drift, arbitrary aggregation and inaccessible measurement can turn MOEs into theatre.

How the property evolved

Original form: Define quantitative objectives and effectiveness criteria for comparing candidate systems. Evolved under criticism into: A small set of validated, decision-bearing measures with provenance, uncertainty and anti-gaming checks; retire measures without consumers.

Evolved form in this source

A small set of validated, decision-bearing measures with provenance, uncertainty and anti-gaming checks; retire measures without consumers.

Ceremony vs property

CONOPS, mission statements, stakeholder registers and workshops are optional carriers. The property is current, authoritative intent that governs and can be challenged.

P006 — Preserve requirement provenance, authority and rationale
Property id

P006

Property name

Preserve requirement provenance, authority and rationale

Historical origin

Requirements traceability lineage; Gotel/Finkelstein pre-specification traceability; current 29148 guidance.

Lineage class

REQUIREMENTS_ENGINEERING_LINEAGE

Tradition relation

CONVERGENT_PROPERTY

Original form

Link each requirement to its source document or stakeholder.

Problem it addressed

A requirement remains active after its source, authority or rationale has changed; a trace link exists but cannot answer why the requirement governs.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

An arbitrary or obsolete requirement consumes design, test and certification effort.

Mechanism

Record source identity/version, issuing authority, rationale, assumptions, conflicts, decision history and validity conditions; challenge provenance before downstream conformance.

Trigger or context

Large or long-lived baselines; regulated/contracted work; reused requirements; multiple issuers; frequent change.

Non trigger or cheap path

For a directly confirmed, low-cost request, source, date and owner may be sufficient.

Dependencies or preconditions

A governed need/source model, identifiable authors/owners, change mechanism and downstream design/V&V consumers.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Requirements must inherit legitimacy from validated need, contract/regulation or explicitly authorised design constraints.

Authority preconditions

Issuing, approving, interpreting and waiving authority must be distinguished.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Each requirement set and relation must identify version, baseline, applicability and supersession.

Interface or integration preconditions

Allocations and cross-boundary requirements require explicit interface ownership and composition checks.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Feasibility and verification method must be considered, while validation remains separate from testability.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: An arbitrary or obsolete requirement consumes design, test and certification effort. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Requirements authority, architect, implementing team, interface owner, change authority, verifier and validator.

Known failure modes

False completeness; ambiguous authority; stylistic compliance; over-decomposition; stale traces; ungoverned volatility; requirement inflation.

Important criticisms

Maintaining rationale is costly and can expose politically sensitive disagreement; source authority can still be illegitimate.

How the property evolved

Original form: Link each requirement to its source document or stakeholder. Evolved under criticism into: Semantic provenance that supports legitimacy and change decisions, not merely backward hyperlinks.

Evolved form in this source

Semantic provenance that supports legitimacy and change decisions, not merely backward hyperlinks.

Ceremony vs property

Templates, shall-statements, databases and RTMs are optional. The property is a justified, current and usable constraint/claim.

Original form

Baseline successively more detailed requirements as understanding matures.

Problem it addressed

Exhaustive upfront specification freezes guesses, while ungoverned iteration erases commitments and breaks downstream consistency.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Teams either lock in the wrong system or continuously churn without a trustworthy current definition.

Mechanism

Maintain maturity states, decision horizons, confidence, open questions and configuration-controlled baselines; elaborate near-term/high-risk requirements first and propagate change.

Trigger or context

Uncertain or novel systems; changing user needs; software-intensive development; long programmes; learning via prototypes/integration.

Non trigger or cheap path

Stable, well-understood repeat work may baseline early and manage only exceptions.

Dependencies or preconditions

A governed need/source model, identifiable authors/owners, change mechanism and downstream design/V&V consumers.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Authority preconditions

Issuing, approving, interpreting and waiving authority must be distinguished.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Interface or integration preconditions

Allocations and cross-boundary requirements require explicit interface ownership and composition checks.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Feasibility and verification method must be considered, while validation remains separate from testability.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Teams either lock in the wrong system or continuously churn without a trustworthy current definition. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Requirements authority, architect, implementing team, interface owner, change authority, verifier and validator.

Known failure modes

False completeness; ambiguous authority; stylistic compliance; over-decomposition; stale traces; ungoverned volatility; requirement inflation.

Important criticisms

Iteration can be invoked to excuse weak analysis; baselines can become expensive freezes or meaningless snapshots.

Original form

Problem it addressed

Ambiguous, conflicting, infeasible or untestable statements pass downstream; alternatively, stylistically perfect requirements are mistaken for correct needs.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Grammar/format compliance masks semantic error or removes useful contextual nuance.

Use quality checks to flag candidate defects; resolve them against source, domain, architecture, interface and V&V evidence; distinguish local statement quality from set/system adequacy.

Original form

Assign priority and manage changes to requirements.

Problem it addressed

All requirements are treated as equally fixed; conflicts and volatility remain hidden until cost, schedule or architecture cannot satisfy them together.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Teams optimise local compliance while sacrificing higher-value or more authoritative outcomes.

Mechanism

Record priority source, conflict sets, negotiation status, volatility, dependency and change cost; revisit after evidence or authority changes.

Trigger or context

Constrained resources; competing stakeholders; evolving markets/missions; architecture trade-offs.

Non trigger or cheap path

When one authoritative requirement set is small and stable, a simple ordered list and exception log suffice.

Dependencies or preconditions

A governed need/source model, identifiable authors/owners, change mechanism and downstream design/V&V consumers.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Requirements must inherit legitimacy from validated need, contract/regulation or explicitly authorised design constraints.

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Teams optimise local compliance while sacrificing higher-value or more authoritative outcomes. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Requirements authority, architect, implementing team, interface owner, change authority, verifier and validator.

Known failure modes

False completeness; ambiguous authority; stylistic compliance; over-decomposition; stale traces; ungoverned volatility; requirement inflation.

Important criticisms

Numerical priorities can create false precision or be gamed by stakeholders; volatility labels can stigmatise legitimate learning.

P010 — Manage assumptions as owned, testable and expiring engineering claims
Property id

P010

Property name

Manage assumptions as owned, testable and expiring engineering claims

Historical origin

Requirements environment/domain distinctions; contract-based design; model-credibility practice.

Lineage class

HYBRID

Tradition relation

HYBRID_RESOLUTION

Original form

Document assumptions underlying requirements and designs.

Problem it addressed

A component, model, trade or reused design works only under an implicit condition that no one owns or rechecks.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Ariane-style reuse, interface mismatch or invalid model inference occurs while all explicit requirements appear satisfied.

Mechanism

Represent each material assumption with owner, source, affected claims, test/monitor, expiry/review condition and response if false.

Trigger or context

Reuse; supplier boundaries; uncertain environment; models/simulation; long lifecycle; autonomous constituents.

Non trigger or cheap path

For local reversible work, state the one or two assumptions that could overturn the decision and test them directly.

Dependencies or preconditions

Defined relation types, owners, source identities, current configurations and real decisions that consume the relation.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Relations must ultimately connect to authorised needs or explicitly bounded engineering assumptions.

Authority preconditions

Someone must be authorised to create, challenge, expire and waive the relation or assumption.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Both endpoints, semantics and validity interval/configuration must be identified.

Interface or integration preconditions

Cross-boundary assumptions require two-sided confirmation and composition evidence.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Material assumptions need a falsification, monitoring or validation plan; trace semantics need sampling/challenge.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Ariane-style reuse, interface mismatch or invalid model inference occurs while all explicit requirements appear satisfied. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Change analyst, maintainer, architect, verifier, integration lead and assurance authority.

Known failure modes

Link-count gaming; stale endpoints; semantically false links; orphaned assumptions; unbounded registers; automation false positives.

Important criticisms

Assumption registers become dumping grounds; unknown unknowns cannot be listed; owners may lack authority to observe the condition.

How the property evolved

Original form: Document assumptions underlying requirements and designs. Evolved under criticism into: Assumption currentness is a first-class relation separate from ordinary traceability, with explicit falsification and change propagation.

Evolved form in this source

Assumption currentness is a first-class relation separate from ordinary traceability, with explicit falsification and change propagation.

Ceremony vs property

Trace matrices and assumption logs are optional. The property is a current, meaningful and challengeable relation.

P011 — Maintain semantic, consumer-driven traceability
Property id

P011

Property name

Maintain semantic, consumer-driven traceability

Historical origin

Requirements-traceability research and standards.

Lineage class

REQUIREMENTS_ENGINEERING_LINEAGE

Tradition relation

CONVERGENT_PROPERTY

Original form

Create bidirectional links among needs, requirements, design, implementation and tests.

Problem it addressed

Links are absent when change-impact or maintenance decisions need them, or present but stale/semantically false.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

A complete matrix gives false confidence while engineers still cannot answer source, consequence or evidence questions.

Mechanism

Define trace types and validity rules around real decisions; maintain selectively; include source/configuration/currentness; sample or challenge semantics rather than count links.

Trigger or context

Many artefacts/teams; high change cost; certification; maintenance; cross-level impact analysis.

Non trigger or cheap path

For small co-located work, deterministic naming, version control and direct inspection may answer the needed question more cheaply.

Dependencies or preconditions

Defined relation types, owners, source identities, current configurations and real decisions that consume the relation.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Relations must ultimately connect to authorised needs or explicitly bounded engineering assumptions.

Authority preconditions

Someone must be authorised to create, challenge, expire and waive the relation or assumption.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Both endpoints, semantics and validity interval/configuration must be identified.

Interface or integration preconditions

Cross-boundary assumptions require two-sided confirmation and composition evidence.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Material assumptions need a falsification, monitoring or validation plan; trace semantics need sampling/challenge.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: A complete matrix gives false confidence while engineers still cannot answer source, consequence or evidence questions. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Change analyst, maintainer, architect, verifier, integration lead and assurance authority.

Known failure modes

Link-count gaming; stale endpoints; semantically false links; orphaned assumptions; unbounded registers; automation false positives.

Important criticisms

Trace maintenance cost, tool fragmentation and collaboration barriers are substantial; automated links can produce false positives.

How the property evolved

Original form: Create bidirectional links among needs, requirements, design, implementation and tests. Evolved under criticism into: A current semantic relation with a named consumer and invalidation rules, independent of spreadsheet or model tooling.

Evolved form in this source

A current semantic relation with a named consumer and invalidation rules, independent of spreadsheet or model tooling.

Ceremony vs property

Trace matrices and assumption logs are optional. The property is a current, meaningful and challengeable relation.

P012 — Justify derived requirements and allocations
Property id

P012

Property name

Justify derived requirements and allocations

Historical origin

Hierarchical decomposition/allocation in aerospace SE; requirements engineering domain/machine reasoning.

Lineage class

DIRECT_SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_LINEAGE

Tradition relation

SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

Original form

Flow system requirements down to subsystems and allocate budgets/functions.

Problem it addressed

Derived requirements acquire authority merely because they appear in a lower-level specification; allocations conflict or erase system interactions.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Subsystems meet their assigned numbers while the integrated system misses mission performance.

Mechanism

For each derivation/allocation, preserve the parent objective, analysis/rationale, assumptions, interface consequences, margin and verification path; reallocate under change.

Trigger or context

Multi-level systems; shared resources; supplier contracts; tight budgets; safety/performance constraints.

Non trigger or cheap path

A small indivisible implementation can keep a direct design rationale instead of formal allocation trees.

Dependencies or preconditions

A governed need/source model, identifiable authors/owners, change mechanism and downstream design/V&V consumers.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Requirements must inherit legitimacy from validated need, contract/regulation or explicitly authorised design constraints.

Authority preconditions

Issuing, approving, interpreting and waiving authority must be distinguished.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Each requirement set and relation must identify version, baseline, applicability and supersession.

Interface or integration preconditions

Allocations and cross-boundary requirements require explicit interface ownership and composition checks.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Feasibility and verification method must be considered, while validation remains separate from testability.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Subsystems meet their assigned numbers while the integrated system misses mission performance. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Requirements authority, architect, implementing team, interface owner, change authority, verifier and validator.

Known failure modes

False completeness; ambiguous authority; stylistic compliance; over-decomposition; stale traces; ungoverned volatility; requirement inflation.

Important criticisms

Top-down flow-down can overconstrain design and conceal emergent interactions; false numerical precision is common.

How the property evolved

Original form: Flow system requirements down to subsystems and allocate budgets/functions. Evolved under criticism into: Allocation is a justified, revisable design decision—not an automatic textual decomposition.

Evolved form in this source

Allocation is a justified, revisable design decision—not an automatic textual decomposition.

Ceremony vs property

Templates, shall-statements, databases and RTMs are optional. The property is a justified, current and usable constraint/claim.

P013 — Identify architecture drivers and quality-attribute concerns
Property id

P013

Property name

Identify architecture drivers and quality-attribute concerns

Historical origin

Systems architecting; architecture-description and evaluation standards; quality-attribute methods.

Lineage class

SYSTEMS_ARCHITECTING_LINEAGE

Tradition relation

SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

Original form

List the requirements and quality attributes that shape system structure.

Problem it addressed

Architecture is organised around component taxonomy rather than the few concerns that actually drive consequential choices.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

A tidy decomposition optimises function while missing latency, evolvability, safety, reliability, human or interoperability trade-offs.

Mechanism

Elicit stakeholder concerns and scenarios, rank uncertainty/consequence, and connect them to architecture decisions and evaluation evidence.

Trigger or context

Multiple quality attributes; high coupling; long-life system; critical non-functional behaviour.

Non trigger or cheap path

For routine low-coupling designs, a short driver list and direct design review are enough.

Dependencies or preconditions

Authoritative intent/requirements, known decision horizon, architecture authority, alternatives and access to relevant domain expertise.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Architectural concerns must be grounded in stakeholder/mission outcomes rather than architect preference.

Authority preconditions

Decision ownership, approval/waiver authority and affected-team participation must be explicit.

Configuration or identity preconditions

The decision, representation and implemented configuration must be related and versioned.

Interface or integration preconditions

Responsibilities, interfaces, shared resources and cross-cutting interactions must be analysed.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Consequential claims require scenario, prototype, analysis, model or integration evidence and reopening conditions.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: A tidy decomposition optimises function while missing latency, evolvability, safety, reliability, human or interoperability trade-offs. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Architecture authority, subsystem teams, interface owners, change authority, integrators, verifiers and lifecycle stakeholders.

Known failure modes

Diagram substitution; post-hoc rationale; stale decisions; local optimisation; arbitrary decomposition; quality-attribute omission; architecture erosion.

Important criticisms

Driver selection can mirror the architect's preferences; quality attributes interact and are hard to quantify.

How the property evolved

Original form: List the requirements and quality attributes that shape system structure. Evolved under criticism into: A current set of decision-bearing drivers with authority, scenarios and measures—not an undifferentiated requirements dump.

Evolved form in this source

A current set of decision-bearing drivers with authority, scenarios and measures—not an undifferentiated requirements dump.

Ceremony vs property

Architecture descriptions, views, boards and models are carriers. The property is consequential structure, rationale, responsibility and evidence.

P015 — Decompose responsibilities while preserving interaction reasoning
Property id

P015

Property name

Decompose responsibilities while preserving interaction reasoning

Historical origin

Large-system design and hierarchical SE; complex-systems critique.

Lineage class

DIRECT_SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_LINEAGE

Tradition relation

SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

Original form

Partition functions/components and assign responsibilities to teams.

Problem it addressed

Decomposition creates local clarity but suppresses cross-cutting behaviour, shared resources and emergent interactions.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Every component passes while the composition fails.

Mechanism

Use decomposition for ownership and tractability, then explicitly model cross-cutting responsibilities, shared resources, modes, feedback and integration hypotheses.

Trigger or context

Many components/teams; organisational distribution; complex interactions; shared budgets or state.

Non trigger or cheap path

Simple low-coupling work may use direct whole-system reasoning without a hierarchy.

Dependencies or preconditions

Authoritative intent/requirements, known decision horizon, architecture authority, alternatives and access to relevant domain expertise.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Architectural concerns must be grounded in stakeholder/mission outcomes rather than architect preference.

Authority preconditions

Decision ownership, approval/waiver authority and affected-team participation must be explicit.

Configuration or identity preconditions

The decision, representation and implemented configuration must be related and versioned.

Interface or integration preconditions

Responsibilities, interfaces, shared resources and cross-cutting interactions must be analysed.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Consequential claims require scenario, prototype, analysis, model or integration evidence and reopening conditions.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Every component passes while the composition fails. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Architecture authority, subsystem teams, interface owners, change authority, integrators, verifiers and lifecycle stakeholders.

Known failure modes

Diagram substitution; post-hoc rationale; stale decisions; local optimisation; arbitrary decomposition; quality-attribute omission; architecture erosion.

Important criticisms

Over-decomposition creates handoffs, duplicate abstractions and false independence; under-decomposition overwhelms cognition.

How the property evolved

Original form: Partition functions/components and assign responsibilities to teams. Evolved under criticism into: Dual representation: clear responsibility boundaries plus interaction/composition analysis and integration evidence.

Evolved form in this source

Dual representation: clear responsibility boundaries plus interaction/composition analysis and integration evidence.

Ceremony vs property

Architecture descriptions, views, boards and models are carriers. The property is consequential structure, rationale, responsibility and evidence.

P016 — Demonstrate modularity, coupling and evolvability rather than merely claiming them
Property id

P016

Property name

Demonstrate modularity, coupling and evolvability rather than merely claiming them

Historical origin

Systems architecting, modular design, change-propagation and architecture-debt research.

Lineage class

SYSTEMS_ARCHITECTING_LINEAGE

Tradition relation

SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

Original form

Partition systems into modules with controlled interfaces.

Problem it addressed

A system is called modular because it has boxes and interfaces even though changes propagate broadly or shared assumptions create hidden coupling.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Promised change independence, reuse or supplier substitutability fails in practice.

Mechanism

Define the change scenarios modularity is meant to support; inspect dependency structure, interface stability, change history and integration evidence.

Trigger or context

Platforms, product families, expected evolution, supplier replacement, parallel development.

Non trigger or cheap path

For one-off short-life systems with little expected change, avoid elaborate modularity analysis beyond obvious fault/change boundaries.

Dependencies or preconditions

Authoritative intent/requirements, known decision horizon, architecture authority, alternatives and access to relevant domain expertise.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Architectural concerns must be grounded in stakeholder/mission outcomes rather than architect preference.

Authority preconditions

Decision ownership, approval/waiver authority and affected-team participation must be explicit.

Configuration or identity preconditions

The decision, representation and implemented configuration must be related and versioned.

Interface or integration preconditions

Responsibilities, interfaces, shared resources and cross-cutting interactions must be analysed.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Consequential claims require scenario, prototype, analysis, model or integration evidence and reopening conditions.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Promised change independence, reuse or supplier substitutability fails in practice. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Architecture authority, subsystem teams, interface owners, change authority, integrators, verifiers and lifecycle stakeholders.

Known failure modes

Diagram substitution; post-hoc rationale; stale decisions; local optimisation; arbitrary decomposition; quality-attribute omission; architecture erosion.

Important criticisms

Modularity can sacrifice global optimisation, create interface overhead and shift coupling into data/operations.

How the property evolved

Original form: Partition systems into modules with controlled interfaces. Evolved under criticism into: Scenario- and evidence-based modularity with measured propagation and explicit cross-cutting constraints.

Evolved form in this source

Scenario- and evidence-based modularity with measured propagation and explicit cross-cutting constraints.

Ceremony vs property

Architecture descriptions, views, boards and models are carriers. The property is consequential structure, rationale, responsibility and evidence.

Original form

Major structural risks emerge only after implementation/integration.

Mechanism

Use consequence-proportionate scenarios, prototypes, models, independent challenge and trade-off analysis; record risks and what evidence would retire them.

Trigger or context

Novel architecture; high consequence; expensive rework; competing quality attributes; uncertain technology.

Property id

P018

Property name

Historical origin

Software technical-debt and architecture-erosion research translated into systems engineering.

Lineage class

SOFTWARE_ENGINEERING_TRANSLATION

Tradition relation

SOFTWARE_ENGINEERING_TRANSLATION

Original form

Track deviations from intended architecture and deferred design obligations.

Problem it addressed

Short-term expedients accumulate hidden future cost while authoritative representations drift from the actual system.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Change becomes progressively slower and riskier; teams optimise around undocumented constraints.

Mechanism

Record deliberate debt with owner, interest mechanism, affected decisions and repayment trigger; detect unplanned erosion through conformance and change evidence.

Trigger or context

Long-lived/evolving systems; repeated exceptions; platform reuse; model/code divergence.

Non trigger or cheap path

Do not create a debt taxonomy for trivial clean-up: fix immediately or record one actionable item.

Dependencies or preconditions

Authoritative intent/requirements, known decision horizon, architecture authority, alternatives and access to relevant domain expertise.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Architectural concerns must be grounded in stakeholder/mission outcomes rather than architect preference.

Architecture authority, subsystem teams, interface owners, change authority, integrators, verifiers and lifecycle stakeholders.

Known failure modes

Diagram substitution; post-hoc rationale; stale decisions; local optimisation; arbitrary decomposition; quality-attribute omission; architecture erosion.

Important criticisms

SE technical-debt evidence is sparse and domain-limited; the label can rebrand ordinary defects or management disagreement.

P019 — Generate real alternatives before consequential commitment
Property id

P019

Property name

Generate real alternatives before consequential commitment

Historical origin

Systems analysis, Hall methodology, trade-study practice and set-based design.

Lineage class

SYSTEMS_ANALYSIS_ANCESTRY

Tradition relation

SYSTEMS_ANALYSIS_IMPORT_OR_ANCESTRY

Original form

Generate candidate systems and compare them before selecting a concept.

Problem it addressed

The preferred option is presented as inevitable, with token alternatives constructed after criteria are known.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Trade studies legitimate predetermined choices and foreclose superior architectures.

Mechanism

Establish a decision frame and minimum diversity of plausible alternatives; include do-nothing/reference options; reveal dominated or infeasible choices transparently.

Trigger or context

Architecture down-select; technology selection; high irreversibility; uncertain solution space.

Non trigger or cheap path

When only one option is legally/physically possible, verify that constraint rather than fabricate alternatives.

Dependencies or preconditions

A legitimate decision frame, decision authority, feasible alternatives, criteria tied to stakeholder value, uncertainty information and decision deadline.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Criteria and constraints must inherit authority from current mission/stakeholder commitments.

Authority preconditions

The analyst recommends; the authorised decision maker decides and owns value judgements.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Inputs, alternatives, evidence and decision version must be frozen enough to reproduce the argument.

Interface or integration preconditions

Cross-system consequences and coupled alternatives must be represented where material.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Claims used to discriminate alternatives need fit-for-purpose data, prototypes, analysis or tests.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Trade studies legitimate predetermined choices and foreclose superior architectures. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Architecture/technology selection authority and stakeholders bearing the consequences.

Known failure modes

Predetermined alternatives; hidden criteria; weight gaming; false precision; stale inputs; analysis paralysis; unrecorded reversibility.

Important criticisms

Alternative generation can consume time indefinitely, and political/contract constraints may make the option set fictitious.

How the property evolved

Original form: Generate candidate systems and compare them before selecting a concept. Evolved under criticism into: Alternative generation is a falsifiable search for materially different feasible means, scaled to decision consequence.

Evolved form in this source

Alternative generation is a falsifiable search for materially different feasible means, scaled to decision consequence.

Ceremony vs property

Trade matrices and formal studies are optional. The property is an honest, uncertainty-aware comparison that changes a consequential choice.

P020 — Test trade decisions for uncertainty, sensitivity and false precision
Property id

P020

Property name

Test trade decisions for uncertainty, sensitivity and false precision

Historical origin

RAND systems analysis, decision analysis, technical trade studies and sensitivity-analysis critique.

Lineage class

SYSTEMS_ANALYSIS_ANCESTRY

Tradition relation

SYSTEMS_ANALYSIS_IMPORT_OR_ANCESTRY

Original form

Score alternatives against weighted criteria.

Problem it addressed

Small arbitrary changes in weights, estimates or assumptions reverse the winner while the scorecard displays a precise rank.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Decision makers mistake arithmetic output for objective truth.

Mechanism

Expose ranges, uncertainty, correlations, non-compensable constraints and rank reversals; test multiple plausible weight/value structures; preserve qualitative judgement.

Trigger or context

Multi-attribute choices; uncertain data; close alternatives; political stakeholder weights.

Non trigger or cheap path

A cheap deterministic discriminator can end the study immediately when one option violates a hard constraint or clearly dominates.

Dependencies or preconditions

A legitimate decision frame, decision authority, feasible alternatives, criteria tied to stakeholder value, uncertainty information and decision deadline.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Criteria and constraints must inherit authority from current mission/stakeholder commitments.

Authority preconditions

The analyst recommends; the authorised decision maker decides and owns value judgements.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Inputs, alternatives, evidence and decision version must be frozen enough to reproduce the argument.

Interface or integration preconditions

Cross-system consequences and coupled alternatives must be represented where material.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Claims used to discriminate alternatives need fit-for-purpose data, prototypes, analysis or tests.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Decision makers mistake arithmetic output for objective truth. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Architecture/technology selection authority and stakeholders bearing the consequences.

Known failure modes

Predetermined alternatives; hidden criteria; weight gaming; false precision; stale inputs; analysis paralysis; unrecorded reversibility.

Important criticisms

Weighted sums invite gaming, double-counting, arbitrary normalisation and post hoc criteria.

How the property evolved

Original form: Score alternatives against weighted criteria. Evolved under criticism into: Sensitivity-first decision analysis with explicit judgement, uncertainty and robustness; matrices are optional calculators.

Evolved form in this source

Sensitivity-first decision analysis with explicit judgement, uncertainty and robustness; matrices are optional calculators.

Ceremony vs property

Trade matrices and formal studies are optional. The property is an honest, uncertainty-aware comparison that changes a consequential choice.

Status at this source freeze

USEFUL_BUT_EASILY_GAMED

P021 — Preserve options, reversibility and decision-reopening triggers
Property id

P021

Property name

Preserve options, reversibility and decision-reopening triggers

Historical origin

Set-based design and evolutionary/iterative engineering.

Lineage class

CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING

Tradition relation

CONVERGENT_PROPERTY

Original form

Delay selection while maturing alternatives and revisit decisions when evidence changes.

Problem it addressed

Premature commitment locks the architecture around immature technology; conversely, indefinite option preservation delays integration.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

A locally rational early choice creates expensive path dependence.

Mechanism

Classify reversibility and option cost; mature high-uncertainty alternatives in parallel where justified; record evidence thresholds and reopening conditions.

Trigger or context

High uncertainty; irreversible manufacturing/infrastructure; immature technology; close alternatives.

Non trigger or cheap path

Low-cost reversible decisions should be made quickly, observed and changed rather than subjected to elaborate option portfolios.

Dependencies or preconditions

A legitimate decision frame, decision authority, feasible alternatives, criteria tied to stakeholder value, uncertainty information and decision deadline.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Criteria and constraints must inherit authority from current mission/stakeholder commitments.

Authority preconditions

The analyst recommends; the authorised decision maker decides and owns value judgements.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Inputs, alternatives, evidence and decision version must be frozen enough to reproduce the argument.

Interface or integration preconditions

Cross-system consequences and coupled alternatives must be represented where material.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Claims used to discriminate alternatives need fit-for-purpose data, prototypes, analysis or tests.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: A locally rational early choice creates expensive path dependence. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Architecture/technology selection authority and stakeholders bearing the consequences.

Known failure modes

Predetermined alternatives; hidden criteria; weight gaming; false precision; stale inputs; analysis paralysis; unrecorded reversibility.

Important criticisms

Set-based methods can multiply modelling/prototyping cost and diffuse accountability.

How the property evolved

Original form: Delay selection while maturing alternatives and revisit decisions when evidence changes. Evolved under criticism into: Economically bounded option preservation tied to learning value and decision horizon.

Evolved form in this source

Economically bounded option preservation tied to learning value and decision horizon.

Ceremony vs property

Trade matrices and formal studies are optional. The property is an honest, uncertainty-aware comparison that changes a consequential choice.

P022 — Assign explicit interface ownership and decision authority
Property id

P022

Property name

Assign explicit interface ownership and decision authority

Historical origin

Aerospace interface-control and configuration-management practice.

Lineage class

CONFIGURATION_AND_INTERFACE_LINEAGE

Tradition relation

SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

Original form

Name responsible organisations for each external and internal interface.

Problem it addressed

Each side assumes the other owns semantics, changes, anomalies or end-to-end behaviour.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Interface defects survive because no actor can authoritatively resolve or rebaseline the relation.

Mechanism

Assign owning parties, approving authority, escalation path, configuration responsibility and shared verification obligations for each consequential interface.

Trigger or context

Supplier/organisation boundary; independent teams; physical integration; SoS; regulated handoff.

Non trigger or cheap path

Within one small team, explicit code/data ownership and direct communication may suffice.

Dependencies or preconditions

Identifiable interacting parties/configurations, shared boundary, owners and a means to test or observe composition.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

External/user/ecosystem semantics must reflect intended operations, not only internal schemas.

Authority preconditions

Each side's authority and the joint resolution/escalation path must be explicit.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Both endpoint versions, contract version and environment must be identified.

Interface or integration preconditions

Physical, logical, data, timing, state, organisational and authority dimensions are considered as applicable.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Interface claims require joint verification/integration evidence under relevant states, limits and failure conditions.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Interface defects survive because no actor can authoritatively resolve or rebaseline the relation. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Interface owners, suppliers, integration lead, architecture authority, operations and change authority.

Known failure modes

Signed-but-stale ICDs; syntactic compatibility without shared meaning; silent change; unowned assumptions; narrow nominal tests.

Important criticisms

Ownership fields can be ceremonial where the owner lacks budget, access or cross-boundary authority.

How the property evolved

Original form: Name responsible organisations for each external and internal interface. Evolved under criticism into: Two-sided ownership with an authority path and joint evidence, not a single document custodian.

Evolved form in this source

Two-sided ownership with an authority path and joint evidence, not a single document custodian.

Ceremony vs property

ICDs, schemas and APIs are optional carriers. The property is shared, current semantics and two-sided composition evidence.

P023 — Specify interface semantics, timing, state and failure contracts
Property id

P023

Property name

Specify interface semantics, timing, state and failure contracts

Historical origin

Telecommunications/aerospace interface engineering; contract-based design; semantic interoperability research.

Lineage class

CONFIGURATION_AND_INTERFACE_LINEAGE

Tradition relation

SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

Original form

Define physical and functional interface characteristics in ICDs.

Problem it addressed

Schemas, connectors or APIs match syntactically while units, meaning, timing, state assumptions, error handling or degraded behaviour differ.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Components interoperate nominally but fail under real sequences, loads or exceptions.

Mechanism

Define units/ranges, semantics, timing/latency, modes/state, protocols, provenance, error/degraded behaviour and compatibility expectations at the necessary precision.

Trigger or context

Cross-team integration; data exchange; real-time systems; safety/performance coupling; supplier APIs.

Non trigger or cheap path

For obvious low-risk local interfaces, executable types/tests and one shared example may be enough.

Dependencies or preconditions

Identifiable interacting parties/configurations, shared boundary, owners and a means to test or observe composition.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

External/user/ecosystem semantics must reflect intended operations, not only internal schemas.

Authority preconditions

Each side's authority and the joint resolution/escalation path must be explicit.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Both endpoint versions, contract version and environment must be identified.

Interface or integration preconditions

Physical, logical, data, timing, state, organisational and authority dimensions are considered as applicable.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Interface claims require joint verification/integration evidence under relevant states, limits and failure conditions.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Components interoperate nominally but fail under real sequences, loads or exceptions. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Interface owners, suppliers, integration lead, architecture authority, operations and change authority.

Known failure modes

Signed-but-stale ICDs; syntactic compatibility without shared meaning; silent change; unowned assumptions; narrow nominal tests.

Important criticisms

Formal contracts can omit relevant environment or human meaning; over-specification can block evolution.

How the property evolved

Original form: Define physical and functional interface characteristics in ICDs. Evolved under criticism into: A current behavioural/semantic contract whose precision is proportionate to risk; documents, schemas, types and tests are interchangeable carriers.

Evolved form in this source

A current behavioural/semantic contract whose precision is proportionate to risk; documents, schemas, types and tests are interchangeable carriers.

Ceremony vs property

ICDs, schemas and APIs are optional carriers. The property is shared, current semantics and two-sided composition evidence.

Interface-control practice refined by mishap evidence and assume/guarantee methods.

Original form

Review and approve ICDs and test interfaces during integration.

Problem it addressed

A signed interface remains stale, one side changes silently, or shared assumptions are never exercised together.

Configuration-compatible components still fail in combination.

Mechanism

Version interface claims; link them to assumptions and owning configurations; perform cross-boundary tests/analysis; monitor change and invalidate evidence on semantic or version drift.

Trigger or context

Frequent interface evolution; independent suppliers; reused components; high-consequence interactions.

Non trigger or cheap path

Stable local interfaces can rely on automated compatibility tests plus change notification.

Dependencies or preconditions

Interface owners, suppliers, integration lead, architecture authority, operations and change authority.

Known failure modes

Signed-but-stale ICDs; syntactic compatibility without shared meaning; silent change; unowned assumptions; narrow nominal tests.

Important criticisms

Maintaining end-to-end tests is costly; test environments may not reproduce operational interactions.

P025 — Obtain cross-boundary interface and integration evidence
Property id

P025

Property name

Obtain cross-boundary interface and integration evidence

Historical origin

Apollo/NASA system-level test traditions and modern interface management.

Lineage class

AEROSPACE_OR_DEFENCE_LINEAGE

Tradition relation

SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

Original form

Test each interface after component delivery.

Problem it addressed

Component-level interface conformance passes while end-to-end flows, timing, modes or organisational handoffs fail.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Late system test discovers composition defects that neither component owner can reproduce alone.

Mechanism

Plan joint evidence at the earliest feasible fidelity, including end-to-end paths, boundary values, transitions, faults and operational actors; retain anomalies and environment limits.

Trigger or context

Critical external interfaces; multiple suppliers; hardware/software/human boundaries; SoS interoperability.

Non trigger or cheap path

For low-risk local interfaces, executable contract tests and one end-to-end smoke path may settle the question.

Dependencies or preconditions

Identifiable interacting parties/configurations, shared boundary, owners and a means to test or observe composition.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

External/user/ecosystem semantics must reflect intended operations, not only internal schemas.

Authority preconditions

Each side's authority and the joint resolution/escalation path must be explicit.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Both endpoint versions, contract version and environment must be identified.

Interface or integration preconditions

Physical, logical, data, timing, state, organisational and authority dimensions are considered as applicable.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Interface claims require joint verification/integration evidence under relevant states, limits and failure conditions.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Late system test discovers composition defects that neither component owner can reproduce alone. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Interface owners, suppliers, integration lead, architecture authority, operations and change authority.

Known failure modes

Signed-but-stale ICDs; syntactic compatibility without shared meaning; silent change; unowned assumptions; narrow nominal tests.

Important criticisms

Shared tests can be brittle, expensive or falsely reassuring if the environment and states are narrow.

How the property evolved

Original form: Test each interface after component delivery. Evolved under criticism into: A risk-ranked interface evidence set tied to both sides' exact configurations and the intended operating context.

Evolved form in this source

A risk-ranked interface evidence set tied to both sides' exact configurations and the intended operating context.

Ceremony vs property

ICDs, schemas and APIs are optional carriers. The property is shared, current semantics and two-sided composition evidence.
