P051 — Design rollback, recovery and change containment for consequential updates
Property id

P051

Property name

Design rollback, recovery and change containment for consequential updates

Historical origin

Configuration/change control, contingency planning and continuous delivery translation.

Lineage class

SOFTWARE_ENGINEERING_TRANSLATION

Tradition relation

SOFTWARE_ENGINEERING_TRANSLATION

Original form

Provide backout plans and contingency actions for changes and releases.

Problem it addressed

A technically approved change cannot be reversed or isolated after integration/operation reveals unexpected effects.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

The system remains in a degraded or unsafe configuration while diagnosis continues.

Mechanism

Classify reversibility, preserve recoverable state/configurations, define stop/rollback criteria, practise recovery where consequential, and bound irreversible transitions.

Trigger or context

Frequent deployment; distributed operations; high availability; uncertain change impact; remote assets.

Non trigger or cheap path

Cheap local reversible edits need only reliable versioning and a known-good state.

Dependencies or preconditions

Governed items, stable identifiers, change authority, status accounting and access to actual product/model/test/environment state.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Configuration must be tied to the authorised capability, commitments and operational population.

Authority preconditions

Authority to baseline, change, waive, release, roll back and supersede must be explicit and consequence-tiered.

Configuration or identity preconditions

This family centrally requires exact item/composition/version/environment/evidence identity.

Interface or integration preconditions

Interface and supplier configuration dependencies must be included in impact and release decisions.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Evidence must cite configuration and be invalidated or justified after change.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: The system remains in a degraded or unsafe configuration while diagnosis continues. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Builder, integrator, release/change authority, verifier, operator, maintainer, supplier and auditor.

Known failure modes

Frozen-baseline bureaucracy; snapshot proliferation; approved-but-unimplemented changes; hidden environment drift; incomplete impact maps; evidence over/under-invalidation.

Important criticisms

Rollback can be impossible for physical changes, database evolution, learned/adaptive state or external ecosystem effects; dual paths add complexity.

How the property evolved

Original form: Provide backout plans and contingency actions for changes and releases. Evolved under criticism into: Recovery evidence proportional to consequence, coupled to exact configuration and operational authority.

Evolved form in this source

Recovery evidence proportional to consequence, coupled to exact configuration and operational authority.

Ceremony vs property

CCBs, forms and baseline reviews are optional. The property is truthful identity, authority, implementation status and evidence continuity.

P052 — Retire stale requirements, models, reviews and controls without live consumers
Property id

P052

Property name

Retire stale requirements, models, reviews and controls without live consumers

Historical origin

Configuration status, technical-debt and model-utilisation criticism.

Lineage class

CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING

Tradition relation

CONVERGENT_PROPERTY

Original form

Archive superseded artefacts while preserving records.

Problem it addressed

Obsolete requirements, models, dashboards, boards and controls remain active, compete with current authority and consume maintenance effort.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Teams cannot distinguish historical evidence from governing information, and process accretion becomes self-sustaining.

Mechanism

Assign consumers and retirement criteria; mark superseded authority; archive provenance; periodically test whether an artefact changes a decision, evidence claim or obligation.

Trigger or context

Long-lived programmes; process layering; model proliferation; changing standards; post-certification evolution.

Non trigger or cheap path

Delete or archive obviously unused low-risk artefacts immediately under ordinary version control.

Dependencies or preconditions

A transparent trigger model, authority to tailor, minimum non-waivable obligations and feedback on actual engineering outcomes.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Consequence and value are judged against current stakeholder/mission commitments.

Authority preconditions

Tailoring decisions require named authority and cannot be self-exemption by the work producer alone where consequence is high.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Applicable lifecycle, product, change and evidence scope must be identified.

Interface or integration preconditions

Coupling, organisational distribution and interface complexity are core escalation triggers.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Evidence fragility, consequence and reversibility determine review/V&V depth.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Teams cannot distinguish historical evidence from governing information, and process accretion becomes self-sustaining. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Technical authority, project/product leadership, assurance authority and teams executing the cheap path.

Known failure modes

Blanket process; arbitrary waivers; size-only scaling; process accretion; inherited controls with no consumer; under-assurance under 'agile' labels.

Important criticisms

Premature retirement can erase future evidence or organisational memory; consumers may be latent or regulatory.

How the property evolved

Original form: Archive superseded artefacts while preserving records. Evolved under criticism into: Lifecycle hygiene: preserve history while withdrawing governing status and maintenance obligations from information with no valid consumer.

Evolved form in this source

Lifecycle hygiene: preserve history while withdrawing governing status and maintenance obligations from information with no valid consumer.

Ceremony vs property

Tailoring matrices and plans are optional. The property is explicit activation/deactivation of engineering machinery by evidence-bearing triggers.

P053 — Include enabling systems and lifecycle stakeholders in system definition
Property id

P053

Property name

Include enabling systems and lifecycle stakeholders in system definition

Historical origin

Lifecycle SE and concurrent engineering.

Lineage class

DIRECT_SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_LINEAGE

Tradition relation

SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

Original form

Plan manufacturing, test, deployment, operation, maintenance, support and disposal alongside the end product.

Problem it addressed

The delivered product works only with unavailable test equipment, untrained operators, fragile logistics or unplanned disposal/support.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Local product optimisation shifts cost and failure into later lifecycle stages or enabling systems.

Mechanism

Model critical enabling systems, stakeholders, interfaces, resources and constraints early enough to influence architecture and evidence.

Trigger or context

Long-lived physical systems; specialised operations; maintainability/logistics; certification; hazardous disposal.

Non trigger or cheap path

For short-lived software/services using standard infrastructure, capture only enabling dependencies that can alter feasibility or operation.

Dependencies or preconditions

Defined lifecycle/system boundary, representative lifecycle stakeholders, dependency/economic rationale and configuration/feedback mechanisms.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Operators, maintainers, manufacturers, support, disposal, regulators and portfolio/mission actors are included only where materially affected.

Authority preconditions

Authority across lifecycle organisations and product-family/mission boundaries must be explicit.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Product variants, enabling systems, operational populations and lifecycle states must be identifiable.

Interface or integration preconditions

Enabling-system, human, platform and mission dependencies are treated as interfaces/compositions.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Operational, maintainability, variability and mission evidence must match the claimed lifecycle scope.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Local product optimisation shifts cost and failure into later lifecycle stages or enabling systems. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Product/mission owner, architect, operations/support, platform governance and lifecycle authorities.

Known failure modes

Unbounded scope; speculative future modelling; commonality overreach; lifecycle stakeholder tokenism; duplication with programme/logistics functions.

Important criticisms

Lifecycle scope can expand without bound; future support/disposal assumptions are uncertain.

How the property evolved

Original form: Plan manufacturing, test, deployment, operation, maintenance, support and disposal alongside the end product. Evolved under criticism into: Selective whole-lifecycle inclusion driven by consequence and dependency, not exhaustive lifecycle documentation.

Evolved form in this source

Selective whole-lifecycle inclusion driven by consequence and dependency, not exhaustive lifecycle documentation.

Ceremony vs property

Lifecycle plans, HSI plans and mission-thread artefacts are optional. The property is early inclusion of dependencies that materially change system decisions.

P054 — Allocate functions and authority across hardware, software, humans and organisations
Property id

P054

Property name

Allocate functions and authority across hardware, software, humans and organisations

Historical origin

Human-systems integration and systems architecting.

Lineage class

HUMAN_FACTORS_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY

Tradition relation

HUMAN_FACTORS_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY

Original form

Assign system functions to people, hardware and software.

Problem it addressed

Automation or organisational design allocates tasks without considering human capability, workload, authority, observability, training or recovery.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

The technical system passes but operators cannot control, understand, maintain or safely recover it.

Mechanism

Treat allocation as an architecture decision with operating context, authority, handoff/interface, performance assumptions and validation with representative users.

Trigger or context

Human-in/on-the-loop systems; autonomy; complex maintenance; high workload; organisational handoffs.

Non trigger or cheap path

Simple tools with direct user control may validate allocation through ordinary use tests.

Dependencies or preconditions

Defined lifecycle/system boundary, representative lifecycle stakeholders, dependency/economic rationale and configuration/feedback mechanisms.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Operators, maintainers, manufacturers, support, disposal, regulators and portfolio/mission actors are included only where materially affected.

Authority across lifecycle organisations and product-family/mission boundaries must be explicit.

Product variants, enabling systems, operational populations and lifecycle states must be identifiable.

Interface or integration preconditions

Enabling-system, human, platform and mission dependencies are treated as interfaces/compositions.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Operational, maintainability, variability and mission evidence must match the claimed lifecycle scope.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: The technical system passes but operators cannot control, understand, maintain or safely recover it. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Product/mission owner, architect, operations/support, platform governance and lifecycle authorities.

Known failure modes

Unbounded scope; speculative future modelling; commonality overreach; lifecycle stakeholder tokenism; duplication with programme/logistics functions.

Important criticisms

This property shares ancestry with human factors; detailed cognitive-fit methods lie outside this lane.

How the property evolved

Original form: Assign system functions to people, hardware and software. Evolved under criticism into: Evidence-based joint human–technical allocation linked to operational validation and change, not a generic 'human factors' checklist.

Evolved form in this source

Evidence-based joint human–technical allocation linked to operational validation and change, not a generic 'human factors' checklist.

Ceremony vs property

Lifecycle plans, HSI plans and mission-thread artefacts are optional. The property is early inclusion of dependencies that materially change system decisions.

Allocate functions and authority across hardware, software, humans and organisations

Applicability

SUPPORTING_OR_NOT_PRIMARY_PROFILE: this property does not create an independent obligation in this profile; apply only where its stated trigger intersects the profile.

Need or source

Operators, maintainers, manufacturers, support, disposal, regulators and portfolio/mission actors are included only where materially affected.

Requirement form

No mandatory requirement form is created by this property.

Provenance

Use the property's source, rationale and configuration identity where it governs a requirement relation.

Assumptions

Defined lifecycle/system boundary, representative lifecycle stakeholders, dependency/economic rationale and configuration/feedback mechanisms.

Authority

Authority across lifecycle organisations and product-family/mission boundaries must be explicit.

Traceability

Maintain only semantic relations needed by a live source, change, implementation or evidence consumer.

Validation precondition

Operators, maintainers, manufacturers, support, disposal, regulators and portfolio/mission actors are included only where materially affected.

Verification precondition

Operational, maintainability, variability and mission evidence must match the claimed lifecycle scope.

Change profile

Product variants, enabling systems, operational populations and lifecycle states must be identifiable.

Cheap path

Simple tools with direct user control may validate allocation through ordinary use tests.

Mature form

Evidence-based joint human–technical allocation linked to operational validation and change, not a generic 'human factors' checklist.

Architecture decision profile
Property

Allocate functions and authority across hardware, software, humans and organisations

Drivers

Current mission/stakeholder outcomes, hard constraints, quality attributes, interface/evolution risks and evidence gaps.

Decision

Treat allocation as an architecture decision with operating context, authority, handoff/interface, performance assumptions and validation with representative users.

Alternatives

Materially different feasible options, including status quo/reference where informative; no token alternatives.

Rationale

Decision context, criteria, evidence, uncertainty, rejected alternatives and consequences.

Assumptions

Owned, current, linked to the decision and given reopening/falsification triggers.

Authority

Authority across lifecycle organisations and product-family/mission boundaries must be explicit.

Configuration

Architecture decision and views/models identify the applicable product/model/configuration.

Evaluation

Scenario, analysis, prototype, model, review or integration evidence proportional to consequence.

Reopen trigger

Changed intent, invalidated assumption, margin erosion, interface/integration evidence, new alternative or configuration drift.

Cheap path

Simple tools with direct user control may validate allocation through ordinary use tests.

Mature form

Evidence-based joint human–technical allocation linked to operational validation and change, not a generic 'human factors' checklist.

Interface assumption profile
Property

Allocate functions and authority across hardware, software, humans and organisations

Interface scope

Physical, logical, data, timing, state/mode, protocol, organisational, authority and environmental dimensions as applicable.

Owner

Both endpoints plus joint resolution/escalation authority; a document custodian alone is insufficient.

Semantics

Units, ranges, meaning, timing, failure/degraded behaviour and provenance are explicit at risk-appropriate precision.

Assumptions

Cross-boundary assumptions are owned, current and testable/monitorable.

Version identity

Endpoint, contract, tool/data and environment versions are bound to evidence.

Change notification

Change impact, compatibility window and revalidation responsibilities are explicit.

Verification

Check each side's conformance to the contract.

Integration

Exercise composition and end-to-end interactions in a credible context.

Degradation

Fallback, error handling and residual incompatibility are represented where consequential.

Cheap path

Simple tools with direct user control may validate allocation through ordinary use tests.

Mature form

Evidence-based joint human–technical allocation linked to operational validation and change, not a generic 'human factors' checklist.

Allocate functions and authority across hardware, software, humans and organisations

Integration profile
Property

Allocate functions and authority across hardware, software, humans and organisations

Integration objective

Expose the highest-value composition uncertainty early enough to change design/action.

Sequence

Risk-, dependency- and learning-ordered rather than merely schedule-ordered.

Verification validation profile
Property

Allocate functions and authority across hardware, software, humans and organisations

Claim

A specific requirement, architecture/interface proposition, model-use claim, mission/use claim or change-equivalence claim.

Verification question

Does the identified configuration satisfy the specified claim?

Validation question

Does it fulfil the current intended use/need in the relevant context?

Method

Test, analysis, inspection, demonstration, simulation, operational evidence or combination selected for discrimination and cost.

Environment and data

Representative enough for the claim; provenance, fidelity and limitations explicit.

Independence

Proportionate to consequence, producer incentives and claim uncertainty.

Coverage and limits

Coverage is stated but never equated with absence of unknown behaviour.

Anomalies

Contradictory and unresolved evidence remains visible.

Currentness

Bound to configuration, assumptions, intended use and change impact.

Cheap path

Simple tools with direct user control may validate allocation through ordinary use tests.

Mature form

Evidence-based joint human–technical allocation linked to operational validation and change, not a generic 'human factors' checklist.

P055 — Govern platform, product-line and variability architecture
Property id

P055

Property name

Govern platform, product-line and variability architecture

Historical origin

Product-line engineering and platform/commonality traditions.

Lineage class

SOFTWARE_ENGINEERING_TRANSLATION

Tradition relation

SOFTWARE_ENGINEERING_TRANSLATION

Original form

Define common assets, variation points and reusable requirements/architecture for a family.

Problem it addressed

Reuse creates untracked variants, incompatible configurations and evidence gaps; commonality is maximised beyond economic or performance value.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

One member's change silently breaks another or invalidates family-wide claims.

Mechanism

Identify variation points, binding time, configuration rules, compatibility, shared/variant evidence and economic/mission rationale; test representative combinations.

Trigger or context

Multiple related products/configurations; long-term reuse; configurable systems; platform ecosystems.

Non trigger or cheap path

A one-off product or two loosely related variants should not trigger a product-line infrastructure.

Dependencies or preconditions

Defined lifecycle/system boundary, representative lifecycle stakeholders, dependency/economic rationale and configuration/feedback mechanisms.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Operators, maintainers, manufacturers, support, disposal, regulators and portfolio/mission actors are included only where materially affected.

Authority preconditions

Authority across lifecycle organisations and product-family/mission boundaries must be explicit.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Product variants, enabling systems, operational populations and lifecycle states must be identifiable.

Interface or integration preconditions

Enabling-system, human, platform and mission dependencies are treated as interfaces/compositions.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Operational, maintainability, variability and mission evidence must match the claimed lifecycle scope.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: One member's change silently breaks another or invalidates family-wide claims. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Product/mission owner, architect, operations/support, platform governance and lifecycle authorities.

Known failure modes

Unbounded scope; speculative future modelling; commonality overreach; lifecycle stakeholder tokenism; duplication with programme/logistics functions.

Important criticisms

Combinatorial explosion makes exhaustive testing impossible; platform governance can constrain innovation and optimise yesterday's variants.

How the property evolved

Original form: Define common assets, variation points and reusable requirements/architecture for a family. Evolved under criticism into: Configuration- and evidence-aware variability management with explicit commonality trade-offs.

Evolved form in this source

Configuration- and evidence-aware variability management with explicit commonality trade-offs.

Ceremony vs property

Lifecycle plans, HSI plans and mission-thread artefacts are optional. The property is early inclusion of dependencies that materially change system decisions.

Status at this source freeze

CONTEXT_DEPENDENT

P056 — Engineer mission/capability relationships beyond a single system when the mission is the unit of value
Property id

P056

Property name

Engineer mission/capability relationships beyond a single system when the mission is the unit of value

Historical origin

DoD mission-engineering lineage and SoS/capability analysis.

Lineage class

MISSION_OR_CAPABILITY_ENGINEERING_LINEAGE

Tradition relation

DOMAIN_TRANSLATION

Original form

Use mission threads and capability architectures to coordinate portfolios of systems.

Problem it addressed

A single-system programme optimises its specification while the mission depends on external systems, doctrine, data and organisations.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Delivered systems meet local requirements but do not create the intended end-to-end capability.

Mechanism

Define mission outcomes, threads, actors, dependencies, measures and change options across systems; preserve authority limits and validate end-to-end effects.

Trigger or context

Defence/civil capability portfolios; mission outcomes span independently managed systems.

Non trigger or cheap path

Ordinary products whose value is directly observable at the product boundary do not require mission-engineering machinery.

Dependencies or preconditions

Defined lifecycle/system boundary, representative lifecycle stakeholders, dependency/economic rationale and configuration/feedback mechanisms.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Operators, maintainers, manufacturers, support, disposal, regulators and portfolio/mission actors are included only where materially affected.

Authority preconditions

Authority across lifecycle organisations and product-family/mission boundaries must be explicit.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Product variants, enabling systems, operational populations and lifecycle states must be identifiable.

Interface or integration preconditions

Enabling-system, human, platform and mission dependencies are treated as interfaces/compositions.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Operational, maintainability, variability and mission evidence must match the claimed lifecycle scope.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Delivered systems meet local requirements but do not create the intended end-to-end capability. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Product/mission owner, architect, operations/support, platform governance and lifecycle authorities.

Known failure modes

Unbounded scope; speculative future modelling; commonality overreach; lifecycle stakeholder tokenism; duplication with programme/logistics functions.

Important criticisms

Defence-heavy lineage, uncertain authority and potential duplication of SoS/portfolio management; outcome evidence limited.

How the property evolved

Original form: Use mission threads and capability architectures to coordinate portfolios of systems. Evolved under criticism into: A mission-level extension activated by genuine cross-system capability dependence, not relabelling every project as a mission.

Evolved form in this source

A mission-level extension activated by genuine cross-system capability dependence, not relabelling every project as a mission.

Ceremony vs property

Lifecycle plans, HSI plans and mission-thread artefacts are optional. The property is early inclusion of dependencies that materially change system decisions.

P057 — Use AI-assisted requirements, architecture and modelling under human, provenance and validation controls
Property id

P057

Property name

Use AI-assisted requirements, architecture and modelling under human, provenance and validation controls

Historical origin

Recent AI-for-RE, AI-for-architecture and AI-for-MBSE research; no settled direct historical lineage.

Lineage class

DIGITAL_ENGINEERING_TRANSLATION

Tradition relation

DIGITAL_ENGINEERING_TRANSLATION

Original form

Generate, classify, link or analyse engineering artefacts with large language models and other AI.

Problem it addressed

Plausible outputs, trace links or models are accepted without source authority, reproducibility, semantic validation or configuration control.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Automation scales hallucination, bias and false coherence into an authoritative engineering baseline.

Mechanism

Constrain use cases; preserve prompts/models/data/tool versions and sources; require domain review, deterministic checks and independent evidence for consequential claims; monitor error and drift.

Trigger or context

High-volume drafting/search; candidate generation; trace recovery; model queries; bounded low-consequence assistance.

Non trigger or cheap path

Do not use AI where a deterministic parser/check/query is cheaper and more reliable, or where outputs cannot be adequately validated.

Dependencies or preconditions

Named model questions/consumers, governance, skilled users, versioning, tool/data access, validation and sustainable maintenance economics.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Models must represent authorised needs/use and disclose omitted stakeholders/context.

Authority preconditions

Authority is claim-specific; tool/repository ownership does not grant truth authority.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Model, metamodel, tool, data, transformation, implementation and physical referent versions must be related.

Interface or integration preconditions

Semantic interoperability, transformation loss, APIs and supplier/tool boundaries must be tested.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Intended use, verification, validation, uncertainty, provenance, currentness and permissible inference are mandatory for consequential use.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Automation scales hallucination, bias and false coherence into an authoritative engineering baseline. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Engineers/analysts making decisions, integrators, V&V authorities, operators and lifecycle data users.

Known failure modes

Model volume; staleness; tool lock-in; inconsistent repositories; semantic loss; perceived-benefit bias; automated false coherence; inaccessible expertise.

Important criticisms

Evidence is predominantly early-stage, laboratory and rapidly obsolete; reproducibility, interpretability, hallucination and governance are unresolved.

How the property evolved

Original form: Generate, classify, link or analyse engineering artefacts with large language models and other AI. Evolved under criticism into: AI as a fallible hypothesis and retrieval/translation aid inside governed SE, never an autonomous authority for need, architecture or assurance.

Evolved form in this source

AI as a fallible hypothesis and retrieval/translation aid inside governed SE, never an autonomous authority for need, architecture or assurance.

Ceremony vs property

SysML, repositories, digital threads and twins are optional technologies. The property is decision-relevant, credible, current and portable structured knowledge.

Property id

P058

Property name

Apply independent technical challenge where consequence and incentive justify it

Historical origin

Independent review, IV&V and programme review traditions.

Lineage class

VERIFICATION_VALIDATION_LINEAGE

Tradition relation

SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

Original form

Convene peer reviews, architecture boards, independent assessment and IV&V.

Problem it addressed

The same team and incentives that produced a decision also certify it; alternatively, independent boards approve without evidence or authority.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Contradictory evidence, optimism and local blind spots survive transition.

Mechanism

Define independence relative to the claim and incentives; give reviewers access, competence, dissent channels and consequence; target high-risk decisions/evidence and record resolution.

Trigger or context

High consequence; irreversible commitment; novel architecture; conflicted suppliers; disputed anomalies.

Non trigger or cheap path

Low-risk reversible work can use peer pairing, automated checks and direct feedback rather than a standing board.

Dependencies or preconditions

Material claim/decision, identifiable incentives and expertise, access to evidence, dissent path, decision authority and proportionality.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Challenge scope must include the stakeholders/mission harmed by false confidence.

Authority preconditions

Reviewer independence and authority to block/escalate/record dissent must be real.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Reviewed claim, baseline, evidence and disposition must be fixed and versioned.

Interface or integration preconditions

Cross-boundary decisions require representation from affected interfaces without letting consensus replace challenge.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Review must inspect evidence adequacy and limitations, not merely work-product presence.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Contradictory evidence, optimism and local blind spots survive transition. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Technical authority, transition/release authority, affected stakeholders and evidence owners.

Known failure modes

Approval theatre; shared assumptions; schedule pressure; understaffing; detached reviewers; duplicated review; diffuse accountability.

Important criticisms

GAO documented review bodies that existed but were ineffective; reviews add delay and can diffuse accountability.

How the property evolved

Original form: Convene peer reviews, architecture boards, independent assessment and IV&V. Evolved under criticism into: Consequence-proportionate independent challenge with real information and decision effect; no presumption that more boards mean more assurance.

Evolved form in this source

Consequence-proportionate independent challenge with real information and decision effect; no presumption that more boards mean more assurance.

Ceremony vs property

Boards, panels and IV&V organisations are optional implementations. The property is consequential, competent and sufficiently independent challenge.

P059 — Feed integration and operational evidence back into intent, requirements and architecture
Property id

P059

Property name

Feed integration and operational evidence back into intent, requirements and architecture

Historical origin

Iterative NASA SE engine, concurrent engineering and agile/operational learning.

Lineage class

HYBRID

Tradition relation

HYBRID_RESOLUTION

Original form

Resolve integration/test discrepancies and update the design.

Problem it addressed

Evidence is treated only as pass/fail against a frozen baseline; discoveries about the need, requirement or architecture are classified away.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Teams fix symptoms while preserving the false premise that generated them.

Mechanism

Allow evidence to challenge every upstream claim under authority control; reopen intent, requirements, assumptions and architecture when observations falsify them.

Trigger or context

Novel systems; progressive requirements; operational pilots; emergent interactions; changed use.

Non trigger or cheap path

A straightforward implementation defect with unchanged premise can be fixed locally.

Dependencies or preconditions

Defined interfaces/configurations, integration authority, suitable environments, entry evidence, anomaly process and feasible sequencing.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Integration must exercise the mission/use interactions that matter, not only convenient assembly paths.

Authority preconditions

Someone must control integration configuration, sequence, facilities, discrepancy disposition and stop/go decisions.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Every integration result must identify products, software/data, environment, tools and configuration.

Interface or integration preconditions

Risky semantic, timing, physical, organisational and state interfaces are first-class targets.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Integration evidence is not automatically verification or validation; claims, coverage and limitations must be stated.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Teams fix symptoms while preserving the false premise that generated them. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Integration lead, architecture/interface owners, V&V authorities, release authority and operators.

Known failure modes

Late big-bang composition; low-fidelity surrogate overclaim; schedule-driven readiness waivers; anomaly closure theatre; component-pass/system-fail.

Important criticisms

Upstream reopening can destabilise programmes and be abused to avoid accountability; contractual authority may resist learning.

How the property evolved

Original form: Resolve integration/test discrepancies and update the design. Evolved under criticism into: A closed learning loop from composition/use to governing intent and decisions, with transparent rebaselining.

Evolved form in this source

A closed learning loop from composition/use to governing intent and decisions, with transparent rebaselining.

Ceremony vs property

Integration plans and readiness reviews are optional carriers. The property is early enough, risk-ranked composition evidence.

P060 — Maintain accessible, current technical data and decision records
Property id

P060

Property name

Maintain accessible, current technical data and decision records

Historical origin

Technical-data management, architecture rationale and digital-thread traditions.

Lineage class

DIGITAL_ENGINEERING_TRANSLATION

Tradition relation

DIGITAL_ENGINEERING_TRANSLATION

Original form

Store and control technical data, models and records throughout the lifecycle.

Problem it addressed

Critical rationale and evidence are inaccessible, duplicated, proprietary, unsearchable or detached from current authority.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Decisions are repeated, suppliers cannot integrate, maintainers cannot diagnose and reviewers rely on presentation summaries.

Mechanism

Identify authoritative records by claim; preserve provenance, access, portability, retention, version and consumer; distinguish governing, working and historical information.

Trigger or context

Long lifecycle; supplier turnover; regulated evidence; multi-tool environment; sustainment.

Non trigger or cheap path

For small work, a well-structured repository with immutable history and clear current pointers may be enough.

Dependencies or preconditions

Governed items, stable identifiers, change authority, status accounting and access to actual product/model/test/environment state.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Configuration must be tied to the authorised capability, commitments and operational population.

Authority preconditions

Authority to baseline, change, waive, release, roll back and supersede must be explicit and consequence-tiered.

Configuration or identity preconditions

This family centrally requires exact item/composition/version/environment/evidence identity.

Interface or integration preconditions

Interface and supplier configuration dependencies must be included in impact and release decisions.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Evidence must cite configuration and be invalidated or justified after change.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Decisions are repeated, suppliers cannot integrate, maintainers cannot diagnose and reviewers rely on presentation summaries. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

Builder, integrator, release/change authority, verifier, operator, maintainer, supplier and auditor.

Known failure modes

Frozen-baseline bureaucracy; snapshot proliferation; approved-but-unimplemented changes; hidden environment drift; incomplete impact maps; evidence over/under-invalidation.

Important criticisms

Central repositories create lock-in and stale duplication; access control can block the very cross-boundary use intended.

How the property evolved

Original form: Store and control technical data, models and records throughout the lifecycle. Evolved under criticism into: Technical knowledge continuity as governed access and identity, not accumulation or one-tool centralisation.

Evolved form in this source

Technical knowledge continuity as governed access and identity, not accumulation or one-tool centralisation.

Ceremony vs property

CCBs, forms and baseline reviews are optional. The property is truthful identity, authority, implementation status and evidence continuity.

P061 — Fixed one-pass V-model or waterfall lifecycle as a universal SE property
Property id

P061

Property name

Fixed one-pass V-model or waterfall lifecycle as a universal SE property

Historical origin

Textbook simplification and conflation of multiple V/Vee lineages.

Lineage class

TEXTBOOK_SIMPLIFICATION

Tradition relation

ONLY_ANALOGOUS

Original form

Complete decomposition/specification once, then implement, integrate and validate once in a fixed sequence.

Problem it addressed

Feedback and requirement change are delayed by process doctrine.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

The lifecycle representation is mistaken for the engineering mechanism.

Mechanism

No retained universal mechanism; preserve only recursive decomposition/composition relationships, early V&V planning and evidence feedback.

Trigger or context

No general trigger. A contract or physical programme may use staged transitions, but that is a context-specific lifecycle choice.

Non trigger or cheap path

Select lifecycle/cadence from risk, reversibility, learning and physical constraints.

Dependencies or preconditions

Not applicable as a retained general property; evaluate the stronger surviving mechanism instead.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

No artefact or process count can substitute for authoritative stakeholder/mission grounding.

Authority preconditions

Approval does not manufacture technical truth.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Ceremonial artefacts often obscure rather than establish current identity.

Interface or integration preconditions

Formal presence does not establish semantic or behavioural compatibility.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Completion/coverage/sign-off is not adequate evidence without a bounded claim, configuration and context.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: The lifecycle representation is mistaken for the engineering mechanism. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

No legitimate universal consumer; retain only context-specific users of the underlying stronger property.

Known failure modes

Bureaucratic accumulation, gaming, false confidence, delayed feedback and tool/process lock-in.

Important criticisms

Modern 15288 is lifecycle-model neutral; historical V lineages were plural and the Forsberg–Mooz Vee addressed concurrent engineering.

How the property evolved

Original form: Complete decomposition/specification once, then implement, integrate and validate once in a fixed sequence. Evolved under criticism into: Iterative, concurrent and recursive SE with context-specific staging and controlled baselines.

Evolved form in this source

Iterative, concurrent and recursive SE with context-specific staging and controlled baselines.

Ceremony vs property

The candidate is itself a ceremony, caricature or overclaim. Any useful residue is represented by another admitted property.

P062 — Exhaustive upfront frozen requirements as a universal optimum
Property id

P062

Property name

Exhaustive upfront frozen requirements as a universal optimum

Historical origin

Contract/acquisition and textbook caricature, not a defensible invariant of RE.

Lineage class

TEXTBOOK_SIMPLIFICATION

Tradition relation

ONLY_ANALOGOUS

Original form

Complete and freeze all requirements before architecture or implementation.

Problem it addressed

Early uncertainty is converted into false certainty and learning is treated as noncompliance.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Wrong assumptions become expensive commitments.

Mechanism

No retained universal mechanism; preserve source/authority, progressive refinement, baseline identity and change impact.

Trigger or context

Only highly stable repeat designs or legally fixed constraints support extensive early baselining.

Non trigger or cheap path

Use minimum sufficient current requirements and test high-risk unknowns.

Dependencies or preconditions

Not applicable as a retained general property; evaluate the stronger surviving mechanism instead.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

No artefact or process count can substitute for authoritative stakeholder/mission grounding.

Authority preconditions

Approval does not manufacture technical truth.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Ceremonial artefacts often obscure rather than establish current identity.

Interface or integration preconditions

Formal presence does not establish semantic or behavioural compatibility.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Completion/coverage/sign-off is not adequate evidence without a bounded claim, configuration and context.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Wrong assumptions become expensive commitments. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

No legitimate universal consumer; retain only context-specific users of the underlying stronger property.

Known failure modes

Bureaucratic accumulation, gaming, false confidence, delayed feedback and tool/process lock-in.

Important criticisms

Empirical RE work shows uncertainty, conflict and change; requirements quality research cannot establish completeness.

How the property evolved

Original form: Complete and freeze all requirements before architecture or implementation. Evolved under criticism into: Progressive requirements with explicit maturity, uncertainty, authority and controlled change.

Evolved form in this source

Progressive requirements with explicit maturity, uncertainty, authority and controlled change.

Ceremony vs property

The candidate is itself a ceremony, caricature or overclaim. Any useful residue is represented by another admitted property.

No legitimate universal consumer; retain only context-specific users of the underlying stronger property.

Known failure modes

Bureaucratic accumulation, gaming, false confidence, delayed feedback and tool/process lock-in.

Important criticisms

MBSE benefit evidence is mostly case/perception; organisational costs and model-quality gaps are material.

P065 — Architecture diagrams as architecture
Property id

P065

Property name

Architecture diagrams as architecture

Historical origin

Document/template simplification.

Lineage class

MODEL_OR_DOCUMENT_CEREMONY

Tradition relation

ONLY_ANALOGOUS

Original form

Produce approved block, context and interface diagrams.

Problem it addressed

Views show boxes and arrows without decisions, concerns, alternatives, assumptions or evidence.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Teams cannot predict change, evaluate trade-offs or explain responsibility.

Mechanism

Retain architecture drivers, decisions/rationale, responsibility, interfaces and evaluation; views are optional projections.

Trigger or context

Diagrams trigger only when they improve shared reasoning or expose structure.

Non trigger or cheap path

A decision record, executable model, table or prototype can carry the property.

Dependencies or preconditions

Not applicable as a retained general property; evaluate the stronger surviving mechanism instead.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

No artefact or process count can substitute for authoritative stakeholder/mission grounding.

Authority preconditions

Approval does not manufacture technical truth.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Ceremonial artefacts often obscure rather than establish current identity.

Interface or integration preconditions

Formal presence does not establish semantic or behavioural compatibility.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Completion/coverage/sign-off is not adequate evidence without a bounded claim, configuration and context.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Teams cannot predict change, evaluate trade-offs or explain responsibility. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

No legitimate universal consumer; retain only context-specific users of the underlying stronger property.

Known failure modes

Bureaucratic accumulation, gaming, false confidence, delayed feedback and tool/process lock-in.

Important criticisms

Standards explicitly avoid prescribing notation/media; rationale research documents staleness and missing knowledge.

How the property evolved

Original form: Produce approved block, context and interface diagrams. Evolved under criticism into: Decision- and concern-centred architecture knowledge with fit-for-purpose views.

Evolved form in this source

Decision- and concern-centred architecture knowledge with fit-for-purpose views.

Ceremony vs property

The candidate is itself a ceremony, caricature or overclaim. Any useful residue is represented by another admitted property.

COMPLIANCE_OR_REVIEW_THEATRE

Tradition relation

ONLY_ANALOGOUS

Original form

An authority signs acceptance after prescribed tests.

Problem it addressed

Authority, politics or schedule converts a bounded decision into a claim that the system is correct and remains current.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Residual limitations, unmet need or post-change invalidation disappear behind approval.

Mechanism

Retain explicit acceptance authority and scope while separating it from verification, validation, residual risk and evidence currentness.

Trigger or context

Acceptance is necessary where ownership/contract transition requires it, but its epistemic scope is bounded.

Non trigger or cheap path

Direct delivery confirmation may replace formal acceptance for small work.

Dependencies or preconditions

Not applicable as a retained general property; evaluate the stronger surviving mechanism instead.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

No artefact or process count can substitute for authoritative stakeholder/mission grounding.

Authority preconditions

Approval does not manufacture technical truth.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Ceremonial artefacts often obscure rather than establish current identity.

Interface or integration preconditions

Formal presence does not establish semantic or behavioural compatibility.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Completion/coverage/sign-off is not adequate evidence without a bounded claim, configuration and context.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Residual limitations, unmet need or post-change invalidation disappear behind approval. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

No legitimate universal consumer; retain only context-specific users of the underlying stronger property.

Known failure modes

Bureaucratic accumulation, gaming, false confidence, delayed feedback and tool/process lock-in.

Important criticisms

GAO cases show programmes can proceed despite weak evidence or unmet user needs.

How the property evolved

Original form: An authority signs acceptance after prescribed tests. Evolved under criticism into: Acceptance as an authorised operational/contract decision supported by, but not identical to, technical truth.

Evolved form in this source

Acceptance as an authorised operational/contract decision supported by, but not identical to, technical truth.

Ceremony vs property

The candidate is itself a ceremony, caricature or overclaim. Any useful residue is represented by another admitted property.

P068 — More reviews and gates as more assurance
Property id

P068

Property name

More reviews and gates as more assurance

Historical origin

Acquisition stage-gate and review-board bureaucracy.

Lineage class

COMPLIANCE_OR_REVIEW_THEATRE

Tradition relation

ONLY_ANALOGOUS

Original form

Add formal reviews, boards and exit criteria to control risk.

Problem it addressed

Review frequency and completion replace evidence quality, independence and decision consequence.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Programmes pass gates while risks, staffing limits or contradictory evidence remain.

Mechanism

Retain knowledge-bearing challenge and transition decisions only where the event changes authority, resources or risk.

Trigger or context

High-consequence/irreversible transitions may justify formal reviews.

Non trigger or cheap path

Low-risk work uses direct peer challenge, automated evidence and rapid feedback.

Dependencies or preconditions

Not applicable as a retained general property; evaluate the stronger surviving mechanism instead.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

No artefact or process count can substitute for authoritative stakeholder/mission grounding.

Authority preconditions

Approval does not manufacture technical truth.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Ceremonial artefacts often obscure rather than establish current identity.

Interface or integration preconditions

Formal presence does not establish semantic or behavioural compatibility.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Completion/coverage/sign-off is not adequate evidence without a bounded claim, configuration and context.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Programmes pass gates while risks, staffing limits or contradictory evidence remain. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

No legitimate universal consumer; retain only context-specific users of the underlying stronger property.

Known failure modes

Bureaucratic accumulation, gaming, false confidence, delayed feedback and tool/process lock-in.

Important criticisms

GAO documented ineffective boards and inconsistent review knowledge; process volume can coexist with failure.

How the property evolved

Original form: Add formal reviews, boards and exit criteria to control risk. Evolved under criticism into: Fewer, evidence-rich and consequence-bearing reviews with explicit dissent and no automatic assurance inference.

P069 — Weighted scorecard as an objective engineering answer
Property id

P069

Property name

Weighted scorecard as an objective engineering answer

Historical origin

Systems analysis and trade-study spreadsheet practice.

Lineage class

MODEL_OR_DOCUMENT_CEREMONY

Tradition relation

ONLY_ANALOGOUS

Original form

Rank alternatives by weighted sums and choose the highest score.

Problem it addressed

Weights, scales, criteria and alternatives are selected to manufacture a preferred winner.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

False precision conceals sensitivity and non-compensable constraints.

Mechanism

Retain explicit alternatives, criteria, hard constraints, uncertainty, sensitivity and judgement; use a matrix only as a transparent aid.

Trigger or context

A matrix is useful when criteria are operational, alternatives comparable and sensitivity shown.

Non trigger or cheap path

Use dominance, hard constraints, direct experiments or qualitative trade reasoning when they settle the decision.

Dependencies or preconditions

Not applicable as a retained general property; evaluate the stronger surviving mechanism instead.

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

No artefact or process count can substitute for authoritative stakeholder/mission grounding.

Authority preconditions

Approval does not manufacture technical truth.

Configuration or identity preconditions

Ceremonial artefacts often obscure rather than establish current identity.

Interface or integration preconditions

Formal presence does not establish semantic or behavioural compatibility.

Evidence or vv preconditions

Completion/coverage/sign-off is not adequate evidence without a bounded claim, configuration and context.

Expected payoff asserted at this source scope

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: False precision conceals sensitivity and non-compensable constraints. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

Decision or consumer

No legitimate universal consumer; retain only context-specific users of the underlying stronger property.

Known failure modes

Bureaucratic accumulation, gaming, false confidence, delayed feedback and tool/process lock-in.

Important criticisms

Cross-domain evidence shows sensitivity analysis is often superficial; stakeholder values may be incommensurable.

How the property evolved

Original form: Rank alternatives by weighted sums and choose the highest score. Evolved under criticism into: Robust, sensitivity-aware decision argument rather than score worship.

Evolved form in this source

Robust, sensitivity-aware decision argument rather than score worship.

The candidate is itself a ceremony, caricature or overclaim. Any useful residue is represented by another admitted property.

Original form

Problem it addressed

Conflicting meanings, models, observations and authorities persist but are hidden behind one system of record.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Organisational or epistemic disagreement is mistaken for a synchronisation defect.

Mechanism

Retain controlled authoritative references by claim, provenance, semantic mappings, inconsistency visibility and adjudication.

Trigger or context

Central reference systems help when many users need identity/currentness.

Non trigger or cheap path

Dependencies or preconditions

Stakeholder or mission preconditions

Ceremonial artefacts often obscure rather than establish current identity.

Reduces the probability, detection latency or consequence of: Organisational or epistemic disagreement is mistaken for a synchronisation defect. It should also improve the quality or speed of the named decision consumer; otherwise it should be retired or simplified.

No legitimate universal consumer; retain only context-specific users of the underlying stronger property.

Bureaucratic accumulation, gaming, false confidence, delayed feedback and tool/process lock-in.

Digital-thread literature reports divergent definitions; model inconsistency may need temporary tolerance.
